Every number on this page is generated by the pipeline, not typed by hand:

```bash
python3 analysis/build_dataset.py        # releases, facilities, LAU join
python3 analysis/build_permits.py        # IED permit linkage
python3 analysis/population_profile.py   # population within 0.5/1/3/5 km
python3 analysis/build_findings.py       # tables, figures, findings.json
```

The machine-readable source is
[quality_report.json](map/data/quality_report.json) (also committed as
`analysis/outputs/quality_report.json`). The flat tables (`facility_year.csv`,
`country_year.csv`, `pollutant_year.csv`) stay in `analysis/outputs/`; the
per-facility downloads on [Findings](findings.qmd) come from the same build.

## Headline checks

{{< include data/tables/checks_summary.md >}}

The carcinogenic-mass check is a reconciliation, not a plausibility check: the
per-facility extraction reproduces the pipeline's country totals to within
0.02 kg over 53,002 facility-years. The site then narrows the definition to
IARC 1/2A/2B (group 3 excluded), which is why the published total is lower than
`country_year.csv`.

## Population coverage

The 2021 JRC-ESTAT grid covers the EU-27 plus Norway and Switzerland. Coverage
is measured against the full 3 km disc: less than 50 % valid cells is reported
as *outside*, 50–99 % as *partial*, and only ≥ 99 % as *covered*. A partial
disc has no published total, because `nansum` over missing cells would silently
understate the count.

{{< include data/tables/checks_population.md >}}

Norway's 3 % coverage is not a bug: most Norwegian E-PRTR facilities sit on
fjords and coastal sites where the 3 km disc is mostly sea, which the grid
codes as no-data. The United Kingdom, Serbia, Iceland and Malta are outside the
grid entirely.

## Permit linkage

| Check | Value |
|:--|--:|
| Facilities linked to a permit record | 20,788 / 32,155 (64.6 %) |
| Linkage among facilities reporting in 2024 | 8,810 / 10,012 (88.0 %) |
| Countries with no records at all | Norway, Serbia, Switzerland |
| Participating countries below 50 % coverage | Denmark, Malta, Czechia |
| Matched facilities with no valid granting date | 19.2 % |
| Matched facilities with no valid update date | 43.7 % |
| Permit rows used (2017–2024) | 477,644 |
| Permit parents absent from E-PRTR | 43,253 |

The linkage is an exact match on `parent_facilityInspireId`. Case-folding and
punctuation stripping were tested and add no matches. One permit per
facility-year is kept: non-empty `permitURL` first, then the latest
`dateOfLastUpdate`, then `dateOfGranting`. `1900-01-01` is the reporting tool's
placeholder and is counted as missing, not as a date.

## What is not in the repository

The two large inputs are kept outside git because of their size:

| File | Size | Where |
|:--|--:|:--|
| E-PRTR release CSVs (v16) | ~100 MB | EEA download, path in `analysis/build_dataset.py` |
| IED permit table F6_1 | 319 MB | EEA download, `EPRTR_PERMITS_CSV` |
| JRC-ESTAT census grid 2021 | 5 GB | JRC download, `EPRTR_CENSUS_TIF` |

Everything the site needs to render is committed: the derived tables, the two
enrichment JSON files and the figures. The build scripts accept environment
variables for the three paths, so a full rebuild does not depend on one
machine's directory layout.
